This PR edited all of these lines to remove the dug-in terms (the omission itself predates the PR). findings.expected: The formula should give the number the page shows. The engine's footing and walking drive are μ × min(m g, what the ground under his feet bears). On sand, Ollie's smaller boots are what decide the contest, not weight.
findings.fix: Wrestle math: 'footing = μ × min(m g, what the ground under his feet bears) (unlimited if bolted)' and 'Drive = min(strength, μ × min(m g, what the ground bears))'. Walking-drive line: 'friction under his own weight (or under what soft ground can bear, if that is less)'. 'Heavier body' line: '...A heavier body wins, unless soft ground caps both.' Arm wrestle math: 'footing = μ × min(m g, ground bearing)'. Wording only; no number changes.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. In the engine, the walking drive is μ·min(m g, Nmax) (pushMatch, engine.js:1530-1533). The footing is anchorCapacity's min(R1, R2), with R2 = μ·Nmax and Nmax = q_ult × 2 × foot area. With the default bodies on Loose dry sand, Ollie's smaller boots give Nmax = 13.6 kN, less than his 29.5 kN weight, so his footing and drive are 7.89 kN, not μ m g = 17.1 kN. The page shows 7.89 kN (verdict, chips, Arm wrestle tile). Its formulas still say 'footing = μ m g' (Wrestle math and Arm wrestle math) and 'Drive = min(strength, μ m g)'. The happens line also calls the drive 'friction under his own weight', so the shown number contradicts the stated formula. The 'A heavier body wins' line is also contradicted: with Ollie set to 3,500 kg against Rex's 3,007 kg on sand, the lighter Rex still walks Ollie out. The omission predates the PR (main said 'μ m g, plus shear × buried area if dug in'). But this PR rewrote exactly these lines, and round 2 fixed the same omission in Sprint (copy-7). Minor: wording only, no number is wrong.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced on its own terms; I could not refute it. src/app.html:70, inside the min-width 920px rule, gives .panel-controls `position: sticky; ... max-height: calc(100vh - 24px - env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)); overflow-y: auto`. Line 3927 opens #setup (Size and density) at 920 px and wider, which the brief requires. With it open, the sidebar holds 1,201 px of content. The box is 694-1,054 px tall, depending on the window.

Page scrolling never moves the box's own scrollTop. It measured 0 at every step of every run. So the box sticks, then leaves the screen with the rig, and its lower part is never shown. That lower part is the Ground menu, the whole Their powers panel (every comic-physics switch and both Bolted switches) and the muscle model.

On main the sidebar had no max-height, so the end of the rig pushed it up and a reader scrolling the page saw both sections. The branch is therefore a regression for page-scrolling readers. It works against brief section 4, which puts Rex + Ollie under Rex's bay so that 'the sidebar stays alongside, so the shared settings, ground and Their powers, are in reach'. It also clashes with the Ollie panel's own pointer, 'His Bolted switch is in Their powers, next to Rex's.' (app.html:374).

The box's cut line falls on a whole control, and its border and rounded corners close it off, so the panel looks complete. The screenshot stuck-branch-1366x768.png shows it ending at the density slider.

With classic scrollbars, a 15 px scrollbar is the only cue. With overlay scrollbars, nothing shows until the box is scrolled. Overlay is the default on macOS with a trackpad, on ChromeOS, and on iPad or Android tablets in landscape at 920 px or wider, where this layout applies.

Other ways in still work: Tab focus scrolls the box, and the wheel works over the sidebar itself. So nothing is fully unreachable. It is a hidden-content regression with no cue, on the page's main settings panel, against an explicit brief requirement. I keep 'major'.

One small correction to the evidence. My first pass seemed to show the Ground menu at 1920x1080, but that came from a loose hit test that also counted ancestor elements. With a strict test (elementFromPoint must be the control or inside it), the branch is null/null at every size, 1920x1080 included. That matches the reviewer. At 1920x1080, #surface spans 1057-1099 px against a box bottom of 1068 px, so at most a sliver of it shows.

A candidate fix was injected into a copy (branch-fix.html) and checked. On first load it shows 'More below: Ground, Their powers ↓' at 1366x768 and 1280x900, and 'More below: Their powers ↓' at 1920x1080. Clicking it brings the Their powers summary on screen and hides the cue. Scrolling the box back to the top brings the cue back. It never shows at 390x844 or at 1280x1400, where everything fits. There was no horizontal scroll and no console errors.
